articleTitle: Examination of Your Skin Hydration System by Observing Your Self-Virtual Avatar's Skin Hydration
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Humectants and humidifiers can be used to prevent dryness in daily life. However, there are problems such as the inability to alleviate the feeling of dryness even when such chemicals or devices are used, the constitution of the body that does not suit the skin to begin with, and environments that do not allow the use of such devices. In this study, we focus on the influence of the Proteus effect on the perception of the body and investigate a system in which the skin of the avatar, which is the body of the user, is moisturized from a psychological perspective by presenting a situation in which the avatar's skin is moistened or looks like it is moistening. For this purpose, this study created an avatar that could be called the user's alter ego, and investigated whether any trends could be confirmed by periodically measuring physiological and psychological changes in the skin condition of a subject viewing a screen in which the avatar exists in three types of environments that seem to moisturize the skin.

articleTitle: Building Serious Game Design to Prepare University Students for The World of Work
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Pandemic hits the world catastrophically, leading to the disruption on our everyday life including how students learn in the pandemic era. Most of the students nowadays have difficulties preparing the way to face the world of work. This research proposes a serious game design to prepare university students for the world of work by combining the Six Facets of Serious Game Design and Adam's Ernest Game Design. Six Facets of Serious Game Design is the design pattern for serious games (e.g., pedagogical games) [1]. Two systems (i.e. the serious game and the baseline system) were designed, deployed and evaluated to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed serious game design. The serious game design was built on an Android mobile phone. Moreover, a simple simulation that has identical scenarios with the serious game was also built as the baseline in the evaluation process. Thirty-seven respondents who will be or have been entering the workplace for their first time participated in the evaluation process. A Wilcoxon rank test was applied to the data as the data does not come from a normal distribution. The results show that the proposed serious game design provides more effective results than the baseline. The user experiences' score provided by the serious game design system is statistically higher than the baseline system. Moreover, the serious game system increases the learners' motivation compared to the baseline system.

articleTitle: Effects Social Media Analytics at Thousand Island (A Case Study Approach)
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: The Thousand Islands is one of the popular tourist attractions in Indonesia, especially for people who want to have a vacation or family in the Thousand Islands. Still, Thousand Islands' social media has yet to be fully used, especially Instagram. This research will conduct social media analysis to increase engagement, especially on the Thousand Islands' social media, Instagram, to improve visitors to the Thousand Islands. This research takes the scope of Instagram and uses secondary data obtained from the Thousand Islands to be analyzed. The paper adopts a descriptive research design for this study. The data collected in support of this work was found using websites such as analisa.io, inflact.com, and manual data mining of Instagram for the third option. The Author has found some results from past data collection in this study. The Author describes the data in the development and discussion section. With the result of this data, the Author checks the data and then summarizes it into a perspective that a researcher can understand. One of the Author's conclusions obtained from the Thousand Islands' social media is that PSO has the highest engagement compared to other social media. PSO social media has an engagement of 1.35%, which proves that this social media often interacts with people on social media and has the most likes and comments.

articleTitle: User Experience Evaluation of The D'Fastint Application using The User Experience Questionnaire
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Interior architecture, a dynamic field meeting evolving community needs, plays a pivotal role in enhancing built environments. D'Fastint, an interior design services provider, developed a mobile app for client interactions. Before its full release, a comprehensive User Experience (UX) evaluation via the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) was conducted. The primary goal was to assess user satisfaction, pinpoint areas lacking in meeting expectations, and plan improvements. The evaluation revealed that the Novelty dimension scored the lowest average (1.234), while the Attractiveness dimension scored the highest (1.677). Overall, users expressed satisfaction, happiness, and motivation with the D'Fastint app. This research provides a novel perspective on interior architecture services and mobile app utilization, addressing unique user needs and preferences. In the context of related works, our study enriches the discourse on UX evaluations and their implications for mobile apps in interior architecture services. It emphasizes the significance of preemptive evaluation and continuous improvement for exceptional user experiences.

articleTitle: User Experience Analysis of the FutureMe Website using the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ)
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: The “FutureMe“ website is a website for sending letters to the future that has a system for writing letters to yourself or other people for a predetermined period in the future. The “FutureMe“ website also contains several collections of letters from other people who are anonymous and contain inspiring emotional messages. In the process of developing the “FutureMe“ website, it is necessary to measure the User Experience (UX). UX measurement is important to do to measure whether FutureMe has met the experience dimensions for users and whether it can be used properly. In this study, we will try to measure and analyze how UX is related to some of the features on the “FutureMe“ website. In conducting UX research on the “FutureMe“ website, the research instrument used was the UEQ (User Experience Questionnaire) or commonly known as the questionnaire technique. The choice of a questionnaire to measure UX on the “FutureMe“ website is because it is very efficient and fast. In this study, we managed to measure the features of the “FutureMe“ website and show what UX dimensions should be evaluated to improve UX on the “FutureMe“ website. The results showed that the website UX system “FutureMe“ excels in the Stimulation scale dimension with a total mean value of 1,492, while Perspicuity is the dimension with the lowest total mean value of 0,980.

articleTitle: Mobile Application Implementation as Agriculture 4.0 Strategy for Sugarcane Yield Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Information engineering strategies play a significant and transformative role in shaping the landscape of digital agriculture. It drives innovation and efficiency in modern farming practices, with a specific focus on enhancing the value of agricultural commodities, such as sugarcane. The application of mobile technology plays a crucial part in achieving increased sugarcane productivity. Mobile applications, equipped with advanced developer features, offer rapid and user-friendly access to vital information. Traditional methods of estimating sugarcane production relied on manual data recording on paper, followed by data transfer to computer systems, typically managed by sugar factory junior plant officers. This conventional approach presents several inherent weaknesses, including time and effort intensiveness during data recording and entry. Additionally, the potential for errors in calculation and data input is a concern. The storage capacity for paper-based documents is finite, and farmers are often unable to autonomously assess their production potential. The objective of this research is to confront these obstacles by creating a sugarcane production application for Android. This application functions as an information engineering approach focused on forecasting sugarcane yields for plantation owners and their assistants. The development procedure adhered to the systematic waterfall method, following the principles of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) model. Data collection was carried out through observations, while interviews with junior plant officers provided valuable insights into sugarcane estimation techniques. Analysis involved the synthesis of observational and interview data to inform the design of the application’s interface and algorithmic system. The resulting application significantly simplifies the process of estimating production potential for farmers, enabling them to access sugarcane productivity data during harvest. Consequently, sugar factories can guarantee both the quantity and the quality of their sugarcane raw materials with confidence.

articleTitle: Investigating Skill Requirements and Gender Bias in Job Openings for Human Computer Interaction Professionals Across the USA, Australia, Germany, India, and South Africa
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) professionals are sought after in the tech industry. Therefore, knowing the specific skills required for HCI talents is important. Our study investigates the skills mentioned in HCI job ads and examines possible gender biases in the wording, analyzing 1247 job ads from the USA, Germany, Australia, India, and South Africa. Our findings emphasize the global demand for technical skills over non-technical ones and reveal differences between the countries, e.g., Germany de-emphasizes communication skills. Notably, feminine-coded language subtly permeates HCI roles. This study provides insights into the skills currently in demand for HCI professionals globally and contributes to our understanding of gendering in job advertisements.

articleTitle: Mood Tracking Apps from the Perspectives of Indonesian Students: A Qualitative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Young people in Indonesia face many challenges related to mental health issues. Social stigma and idealistic upbringing discourage many from expressing their emotions and struggles. Mood tracking apps have been known to help people in understanding their wellbeing. Moreover, self-monitoring can facilitate early intervention. This study seeks to comprehend the perspectives of Indonesian students regarding the use of mood monitoring apps. We asked first-year students to use readily available mood tracking apps and discuss their preferences through two sessions of Focus Group Discussion (FGD) held in March and April 2023 for one week per session. Each FGD session lasted approximately two hours. We identified six main themes using inductive thematic analysis: customization of content, display, and settings, self-assessment, ease of use, social connection, accessibility, and motivation. Participants highlighted the need for specialized icons for their campus experience, Indonesian language option, as well as data and features related to their courses and assignments. Our findings have the potential to help both researchers and designers create better mood tracking apps for Indonesian students.

articleTitle: Exploratory Study on User Experience (UX) of Public E-Procurement System in Malaysia: A Qualitative Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: The public e-Procurement system in Malaysia is a crucial component of the e-Government services. Its primary function is to provide a platform for government agencies to efficiently procure goods and services from business users. The user experience (UX) of this e-Procurement system has emerged as a pivotal factor in the success of the broader e-Government digital transformation. Ensuring that the digitalization of the public e-Procurement system aligns with its objectives and delivers a top-tier Government Electronic Procurement System is imperative. This research aims to gain a comprehensive understanding of the UX issues and challenges faced by stakeholders when using the public e-Procurement system. The study employs a qualitative approach, delving into the perspectives and insights of e-Procurement system users. Data from interview sessions involving nine (9) participants have been meticulously interpreted, coded, and subjected to thematic analysis, revealing five distinct dimensions of issues and challenges: usability, performance, operational, quality, and user satisfaction. To address these identified concerns, we proposed several recommendations. Enhancements in system user interface (UI), navigational aspects, system features, performance, and operational aspects are essential to ensure sustained quality and user satisfaction within the e-Procurement system. The study also explores avenues for future work to further refine and augment these improvements.

articleTitle: Assessment of the Monitor System Interface: A Setup System Tool for Industrial Exoskeletons
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Workers in industries are prone to injuries and musculoskeletal disorders when performing normal tasks. A potential solution to alleviate this situation is the use of back-support industrial exoskeletons in the workplace. These wearable devices consist of electrical actuators, sensors, and controllers that produce appropriate assistive forces when workers complete their activities. The technological integration of different active components in the exoskeleton creates a complex system with multiple strategies to achieve the force modulation produced by the system. In these scenarios, it is important to open some domains of the exoskeleton to the user to initialize the system, calibrate the exoskeleton, introduce user personal information (such as weight and height), and modify the controller parameters. The work presented in this study shows the assessment of the monitor system interface, which is a graphical user interface that allows the user to interact directly with the exoskeleton domains with easy adjustments. XoTrunk is an active industrial exoskeleton designed for carrying and lifting tasks. The controller architecture permits adequate force modulation according to the user action with an adjustable control strategy from the monitor system interface. Experiments were conducted with 12 participants in a standard lifting action wearing the exoskeleton. The results showed that the monitor system interface is a useful tool for human-robot interaction. The current version of the interface grants the user access to the exoskeleton domains previously mentioned.

articleTitle: Enhancing Children's Health Awareness through Narrative Game-Based Learning using Digital Technology: A Framework and Methodology
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Effective health education and awareness initiatives are essential in a world facing growing concerns about children's well-being and rising unhealthy behaviours. This research presents a Narrative Game-Based Learning (N-GBL) framework designed to enhance children's health awareness, addressing critical gaps in their health education. Through a systematic literature review following the PRISMA methodology, this study identifies 13 essential components that form the foundation of the N-GBL framework. These components are structured around the Input-Process-Output (IPO) model, emphasizing narratives, game mechanics, and user engagement strategies. The core purpose of the N-GBL framework is to deepen children's understanding of the consequences of their choices, fostering informed decision-making and to empower them to make healthier choices. This research contributes to developing effective health awareness games tailored to children's learning preferences, bridging existing gaps in their health education. The N-GBL framework offers a revolutionary approach to health education for children, significantly enhancing health awareness and reducing health issues resulting from unhealthy behaviours. Future work will involve expert validation and practical testing in primary schools to transform health education for children.

articleTitle: A React Style Guide Library for MUI Web Apps
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: A Graphical User Interface is a resource that enables users to interact with applications and relies on consistent and standardized user experience, usually defined in style guide documents. This document is important not only to developers and designers but also for the project owners, who are able to better understand the look and feel of the expected software. Often, this document is not available or needs to be rebuilt from the running system itself. To solve this common issue, this paper proposes an automated style guide generation tool for React.js projects with Material UI, including information on typography, color palette, spacing, and other user interface elements. The proposed tool was applied to two in-house projects and three open-source ones to generate style guide documents, achieving success. We found that it is a useful tool that provides a fast, reliable, and up to date style guide document for the participating teams.

articleTitle: Humans + AI: Exploring the Collaboration Between AI and Human Labor in the Workplace
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies have seen an increase in usage in varying sectors of society due to their ability to efficiently find solutions to highly complex problems. This led to the growing concern among the workforce that fully automated AI systems may displace a significant portion of low-wage and low-skilled jobs. The 5th Industrial Revolution (5IR) promotes the concept of augmented intelligence where there is evident collaboration between humans and AI machines. Augmented intelligence enhances rather than replaces human abilities through a more harmonious working relationship that leads to increased productivity. This study investigates employers' and workers' perception of how augmented intelligence is currently practiced in the Philippine workplace to improve task performance. It explores the adaptation strategies of human workers to co-exist with intelligent machines in the workplace. Findings from this study can shed insights on AI integration in task performance and facilitate the adoption of workplace practices that encourage humans to maximize the potential benefits afforded by AI systems as we move towards a more technology-driven work environment.

articleTitle: Chatbots as Peer Counselors in Helping Students Manage Stress: Socio-Technical Requirements
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Pressure to perform well academically and to sustain positive relationships with family and friends cause varying degrees of stress among students that can affect their performance and impact their mental health and well-being. A known solution in reducing stress is through peer counseling where experiences and hardships are shared with trusted peers in order to extend and receive support from one another. Insufficient number of trained peer counselors, however, limit its contribution. The capabilities offered by chatbots has sparked recent interest in their potential usage as an accessible healthcare technology to help individuals cope with stress and manage their well-being. In this study, interviews with senior high students from a private university in Manila were conducted to identify the causes of their stress, determine the strategies they employed in managing stress with particular emphasis on peer counseling, and solicit feedback on their perception of a peer counselor chatbot. Findings from this study can provide insights on the ideal characteristics of a chatbot as a peer counselor and inform future designers of such technologies to help in stress management towards maintaining good mental health and well-being.

articleTitle: Digital Interactive Game Interfaces for Elderly: Digital Drumming Games as Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted lifestyle habits, pushed people to overcome spatial limitations, and enjoy the benefits of home interactions through physical or online interactions. Adapting to the life development of the elderly, given their physiological, psychological, and social changes, is a critical challenge in addressing the rapidly aging population. Digital games contain many features; however, many digital games lack age-specific design, creating usability challenges for the elderly. Hence, interfaces catering to their needs are essential to enhancing their adoption and usage. Based on the above-mentioned, the research objectives are as follows: (1) Conduct a literature review and collate a comprehensive set of interface design principles suitable for the elderly. (2) Develop a digital interactive game that enhances home interactions for the elderly. The scope of the study focuses on tablet devices, so it is not applicable to other digital devices. The positive effects of digital game use among the elderly, interface design guidelines and related development theories, as well as the benefits of drumming are examined by a review of the relevant literature. Focus group interviews were used to summarize and encode experts' recommendations, which were combined with literature review to form interface design principles that were used to develop game prototypes.

articleTitle: Efficacy Comparison of Augmented Reality and Virtual Reality-based Games for Post-Stroke Rehabilitation: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: The usage of Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR) games is seen to have the potential to deliver considerable advantages for post-stroke rehabilitation since it can increase healing progress while saving time and money. This study compares the use of AR and VR in games for post-stroke rehabilitation by assessing the game design, measurement technique, and challenges that may be improved for future studies. Using the PRISMA concept to conduct a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) of related research by identifying relevant data sources, evaluating abstracts, determining eligible publications, and analyzing data using the meta-analysis approach. We analyzed 198 publications from multiple database sources during this procedure and identified 24 papers for additional investigation. The study's implications show that the game design and assessment technique that best meets post-stroke rehabilitation assignments is the most important aspect in assessing the capabilities of AR and VR games for post-stroke rehabilitation, which influences future research on AR and VR games. It was also discovered that numerous obstacles to the usage of AR and VR games must be solved in order to maximize the post-stroke recovery process. However, the data sources employed in the study have limitations. To optimize the utilization of AR and VR games in post-stroke rehabilitation, it is required to examine rules and infrastructure, as well as to employ more diverse data sources.
